item.title: The MAESTRO turbulence dataset derived from the SAFIRE ATR42 aircraft
item.description:
The MAESTRO turbulence dataset derived from the SAFIRE ATR42 aircraft
Louis Jaffeux, Marie Lothon, Fleur Couvreux, Dominique Bouniol, Grégoire Cayez, Lilian Joly, Jérémie Burgalat, Cyrille De Saint Leger, Hubert Bellec, Olivier Henry, Dyaa Chbib, Tetyana Jiang, Vergez Gilles, and Sandrine Bony
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8229–8253, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8229-2026, 2026
A new dataset from the MAESTRO airborne campaign over the tropical Atlantic near Cabo Verde offers detailed turbulence measurements of temperature, moisture, and wind. The data was processed exploiting exceptional instrumental redundancy to provide best quality turbulence statistics and ensure their reliability. This resource can benefit weather and climate models by providing a clearer picture of how turbulence below clouds influences their formation and organization.

item.title: A new global dataset of photosynthesis parameters
item.description:
A new global dataset of photosynthesis parameters
Žarko Kovač, Marija Bačeković Koloper, Shubha Sathyendranath, Gemma Kulk, Heather Bouman, and Leon Ćatipović
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8255–8274, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8255-2026, 2026
Marine life depends on photosynthesis, but models of ocean productivity require measurements that are scarce and costly. We developed a method to estimate how microscopic marine plants use light from existing measurements of production at different depths. Applying it to global ocean observations, we recovered 3776 sets of photosynthesis parameters and created a publicly available dataset. This resource can improve estimates of ocean productivity and its role in the global carbon cycle.

item.title: A 1 km gridded dataset of Northern Hemisphere permafrost active layer thickness (2000–2024)
item.description:
A 1 km gridded dataset of Northern Hemisphere permafrost active layer thickness (2000–2024)
Yujiao Wei, Zhaoqi Wu, Jiaxue Wang, Huanfeng Shen, and Yiyun Chen
Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 8211–8227, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-8211-2026, 2026
Thawing permafrost accelerates global warming and threatens infrastructure, yet tracking changes over vast areas remains difficult. We combined over two decades of ground observations with artificial intelligence to create a continuous, highly detailed yearly map of permafrost thaw depth across the Northern Hemisphere from 2000 to 2024. Overcoming previous mapping limitations, this reliable dataset provides a vital tool to evaluate environmental hazards and protect vulnerable regions.

item.title: High-Elevation Meteorological Datasets from the Quelccaya Ice Cap and Surrounding Sites in the Cordillera Vilcanota, Peru: 2012–2026
item.description:
High-Elevation Meteorological Datasets from the Quelccaya Ice Cap and Surrounding Sites in the Cordillera Vilcanota, Peru: 2012–2026
L. Baker Perry, Arbindra Khadka, Ludving Cano, Anton Seimon, Tom Matthews, Sandro Arias, Heather Guy, Maxwell Rado, Nilton Montoya, Courtney Cooper, and Wilson Suarez
Earth Syst. Sci. Data Discuss., https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-839,2026
Preprint under review for ESSD (discussion: open, 0 comments)
We present quality-controlled meteorological datasets collected during 2012–2026 from five automatic stations spanning 4,895–6,349 m in Peru’s Cordillera Vilcanota. Measurements include temperature, humidity, wind, pressure, snow height change, solar irradiance, and precipitation, complemented by snow pit observations and upper-air soundings. These datasets support research on climate–glacier interactions, environmental change, and past climates.
